build.title: Retire Build Manager: the orchestrator is the only place that browses and manages builds (tabs, planned + final account pick, 5-min account health check)

said.text: Get rid of build manager. Remove it. Uninstall it. If it has responsibilities, decide who to hand them to. The only thing that browses or manages builds is the orchestrator. Tabs: pending, active, incomplete, complete, errors, queue. He has to split it right away so the queue can show the steps. He'll plan what model, what account. When the time comes up in the queue he makes his final decision and updates which subscription took it. Subscriptions first, then any API. Every five minutes a background headless session that doesn't affect any builds or sign anything out checks all the accounts: can get in, have credits, can accept the Fable model.

# Build: retire-build-manager-the-orchestrator-is-the-onl

## Brett said (verbatim)
At: 2026-11-10T15:29:42.107Z
> Get rid of build manager. Remove it. Uninstall it. If it has responsibilities, decide who to hand them to. The only thing that browses or manages builds is the orchestrator. Tabs: pending, active, incomplete, complete, errors, queue. He has to split it right away so the queue can show the steps. He'll plan what model, what account. When the time comes up in the queue he makes his final decision and updates which subscription took it. Subscriptions first, then any API. Every five minutes a background headless session that doesn't affect any builds or sign anything out checks all the accounts: can get in, have credits, can accept the Fable model.

## What to build
Continue build "Retire Build Manager: the orchestrator is the only place that browses and manages builds (tabs, planned + final account pick, 5-min account health check)" (retire-build-manager-the-orchestrator-is-the-onl) — Phase 1, model Opus.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-10 15:29):
"Get rid of build manager. Remove it. Uninstall it. If it has responsibilities, decide who to hand them to. The only thing that browses or manages builds is the orchestrator. Tabs: pending, active, incomplete, complete, errors, queue. He has to split it right away so the queue can show the steps. He'll plan what model, what account. When the time comes up in the queue he makes his final decision and updates which subscription took it. Subscriptions first, then any API. Every five minutes a background headless session that doesn't affect any builds or sign anything out checks all the accounts: can get in, have credits, can accept the Fable model."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Steps in this phase (3 left, ~1.3 h):
[ ] s1 (~30 min) Uninstall/remove the Build Manager plugin. Audit its responsibilities first and hand each to the orchestrator (or the right owner); nothing lost. Supersedes split-builds-pages-build-manager-pending-complet-2. 2) Orchestrator screen tabs: Pending (everything it's been asked to do), Queue, Active, Incomplete, Complete, Errors. 3) Splitting happens right away when a build is filed, so the Queue shows steps. At that point the orchestrator plans model + account. When the build's turn comes in the queue it makes the final account decision and records which account took it. 4) Account pick: subscriptions first (any subscription), then any API account, moving on until one accepts, if what it believed about an account turns out wrong. 5) Account health: every 5 minutes a background check (headless, never touches running builds, never signs anything out) confirms each account can sign in, has credits, and can run the needed model (Fable). The orchestrator always knows every account's status from this, so it doesn't test at dispatch time. Note: reconcile with the Claude Accounts Manager plugin's drag-and-drop account order. Full API control.
[ ] s2 (~30 min) Get rid of build manager. Remove it. Uninstall it. If it has responsibilities, decide who to hand them to. The only thing that browses or manages builds is the orchestrator. Tabs: pending, active, incomplete, complete, errors, queue. He has to split it right away so the queue can show the steps. He'll plan what model, what account. When the time comes up in the queue he makes his final decision and updates which subscription took it. Subscriptions first, then any API. Every five minutes a background headless session that doesn't affect any builds or sign anything out checks all the accounts: can get in, have credits, can accept the Fable model.
[ ] s3 (~20 min) Tests green, report _claude/builds/reports/retire-build-manager-the-orchestrator-is-the-onl.md, THREADS row, commit, push, PR
Read first: _claude/builds/reports/retire-build-manager-the-orchestrator-is-the-onl.md, _claude/THREADS.md
Tick each step: node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs act step retire-build-manager-the-orchestrator-is-the-onl <stepId> done — it reaches main at once (builds-live). Link your branch / PR: node framework/cli/builds-live.mjs link retire-build-manager-the-orchestrator-is-the-onl --branch <b> --pr <n>.
Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.
Screenshots that are not for approval (checking a screen, live captures, before/after): axf shot <file> --name "…" --app … --screen … --group "<build name>" (UI Review → Screenshots; ui-review-item@1), never the review queue.

## Pipeline
This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account mossesx-max- for the Opus phase. Tick every step as you finish it (orchestrator.mjs act step retire-build-manager-the-orchestrator-is-the-onl <stepId> done). When this phase's steps are done, stop: the dispatcher starts the next phase on the right account. If you must stop early with steps left, say why in a build note (orchestrator.mjs act note retire-build-manager-the-orchestrator-is-the-onl "…"); the build goes back to Pending for Brett.
